text:
Priya Shah  09:06
Hey folks — Support requesting we declare a formal incident (or at least run incident process) for elevated 5xx on Hosted in eu-west. Seeing a spike since ~08:47. Multiple enterprise tickets now, and we have at least one customer pinned to `rw-llama-70b-instruct-2025-12-18` getting intermittent `502/503`.

Signals:
- Support queue: 6 separate threads referencing eu-west 5xx in last 20m
- Error examples from customer logs:
  - `status=503 upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers. reset reason: connection termination`
  - `status=502 bad gateway` from `/v1/chat/completions`
- Sample request ids: `req_7gH2mQ...`, `req_7gH3B1...`, `req_7gH3Kp...`
- Impact: prod traffic, user-facing errors. We’re already giving retry guidance but failures persist.

Can SRE confirm if this meets incident threshold? We need comms cadence aligned ASAP. :rotating_light:

Dev Patel  09:07
+1. This is already “incident-adjacent” in terms of customer impact. If we don’t declare, we still need a single owner + update rhythm we can mirror to customer threads. What’s the current eu-west 5xx rate vs baseline?

Rafael Mendes  09:09
Looking. Checking API gateway 5xx + runtime upstream in eu-west now.

Tomáš Novák  09:11
Before we page half of oncall: are we seeing broad regional degradation or just that pinned model version? (Trying to avoid incident churn if it’s a single deployment shard.)

Priya Shah  09:12
From Support view: mixed models. The pinned model example is the loudest enterprise ticket, but I’m also seeing defaults failing (not just pinned). Customers reporting “random 5xx then succeeds on retry”, but it’s frequent enough to trip their SLOs.

incident-bot  09:13
Detected keyword: "declare incident".
If you want to start incident workflow, reply with:
`/incident start`
Or create an incident draft:
`/incident draft`

Miles Thornton  09:13
If we do this, please use the workflow so we get the required fields + auto-thread in #incidents. (This is exactly the case the support escalation flow is meant for.)

Rafael Mendes  09:15
Current metrics (eu-west):
- API gateway: 5xx at ~1.8% over last 15m (baseline ~0.2%)
- Runtime upstream 5xx: ~1.1% over last 15m
- Latency also up (p95 +40-60%)
Not isolated to a single model, but the spike is heavier on `rw-llama-70b-*` routes.

Sean Gallagher  09:16
Given it’s >1% 5xx sustained + multiple enterprise customers reporting production impact, this qualifies for incident process. Let’s declare and keep it tight (single incident channel + one comms source of truth).

Dev Patel  09:16
Thanks. I’ll mirror to customer threads once we have incident ID + comms cadence. Also: can we confirm whether status page post is warranted? (Support keeps getting asked if this is “known outage”.)

Sean Gallagher  09:17
We can start internal incident immediately. Status page depends on confirmation of broad customer impact; with 1.8% 5xx and multiple reports, I lean yes (at least “Investigating” for eu-west API). Rafael, what’s blast radius by org count?

Rafael Mendes  09:18
Org count impacted (non-zero 5xx) in last 15m: ~47 orgs in eu-west, includes several top-tier. That’s not just one customer.

Tomáš Novák  09:18
Ok that’s enough. Let’s not overthink. Start incident, assign IC, then we can decide status page within first update.

Priya Shah  09:19
Running the workflow now.

Priya Shah  09:19
/incident start

incident-bot  09:19
Starting incident workflow…
1) Severity (Sev0-Sev3)?
2) Service/region?
3) Customer impact summary?
4) Primary symptoms (metrics + examples)?
5) Initial owner/IC?
6) Comms channel (status page yes/no)?

Priya Shah  09:20
1) Sev1 (customer-facing errors, multi-org, no data loss)
2) Hosted API – eu-west
3) Elevated 5xx (502/503) for chat completions + increased latency; multiple enterprise and self-serve orgs impacted
4) 5xx ~1.8% (baseline 0.2%), upstream 5xx ~1.1%, p95 latency up 40-60%; sample request ids above
5) IC: Rafael Mendes (SRE oncall)
6) Status page: recommend yes (Investigating) pending IC confirmation

incident-bot  09:20
Incident created: INC-2387
IC: Rafael Mendes
War room: #inc-inc-2387
Doc: https://redwood-inference.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INC/pages/INC-2387
Next steps:
- Post initial update within 10 minutes
- Assign Comms + Ops roles
- Add customer-facing update template reminders

Miles Thornton  09:21
Nice. :thumbsup: I’ll drop the comms template reminder into the incident channel.

Owen Phillips  09:22
Support question: can we get an “approved to share” blurb now? We need something consistent across ~6 open tickets. Folks are already asking for ETA.

Sean Gallagher  09:23
Approved language (safe):
“We’re investigating elevated error rates for requests in eu-west. Our engineering team is engaged and we’ll provide updates every 30 minutes until mitigated. In the meantime, retries with exponential backoff may succeed.”
No ETA. Don’t promise resolution time. If they ask, say we’ll share mitigation progress as soon as we have it.

Dev Patel  09:24
What update cadence do we want Support to mirror? 30 min works for enterprise; for self-serve tickets we can do “next update in ~60 min unless status changes.”

Rafael Mendes  09:25
For incident: first update in 10 min, then every 30 min while elevated. If we mitigate earlier, we’ll post immediately. Support can mirror 30 min for enterprise + “significant change” for self-serve.

Tomáš Novák  09:26
Also: please keep the “incident vs support escalation” boundary clear in tickets. This one is clearly incident-level due to multi-org + elevated error rate. But we should avoid turning every single-customer intermittent 5xx into a formal incident.

Priya Shah  09:27
Understood. For this thread: I’ll reply in the open tickets with the approved blurb + link to status page once it’s up.

Miles Thornton  09:28
Posting reminder here too for visibility — comms checklist:
- Don’t mention internal hypotheses (“maybe noisy neighbor”, “maybe rollout”) until confirmed
- Ask customers for request ids + timestamps + region + model + SDK version
- If they can fail over region, only suggest if their data residency allows and they’re not pinned to eu-west-only requirements

Dev Patel  09:29
One more: should we recommend customers temporarily pin a different model revision / or remove pinning? We’ve got at least one pinned model customer.

Rafael Mendes  09:31
Not yet. We don’t know if it’s model-specific vs regional infra. For now: retries + increase client timeout to 60s + streaming reconnect if applicable. If we identify a bad shard/model deployment, we’ll provide a targeted workaround.

Sean Gallagher  09:33
Agree. Also, any customer comms about region failover needs Security/CS signoff for enterprise accounts (data locality).

Owen Phillips  09:34
Got it. We’ll stick to retries/backoff and “investigating”.

Priya Shah  09:36
For tracking: I’ll tag the existing tickets as “INC-2387” and consolidate duplicates. If anyone wants specific ticket links, DM me.

incident-bot  09:40
Reminder: Next incident update due in 5 minutes (INC-2387). Use `/incident update` to post.

Rafael Mendes  09:44
Update posted in #inc-inc-2387: initial mitigation in progress (traffic shifting within eu-west + gateway pool recycle). Status page set to Investigating.

Dev Patel  09:45
Thanks. I’ll mirror:
- Enterprise: update every 30 min with “still investigating / mitigation in progress”
- Self-serve: point to status page + “we’ll update if status changes”

Tomáš Novák  09:47
Please make sure the status page copy stays generic (“elevated errors in eu-west API”). Don’t mention specific customers, pinned versions, or internal component names.

Priya Shah  09:48
Ack. Using generic language only.

Miles Thornton  10:05
FYI we should capture this as a known-issues candidate if it ends up being a specific eu-west routing/gateway behavior (workaround: region fallback / adjust timeouts). But let’s wait for RCA.

Rafael Mendes  10:26
Quick note here: error rate is dropping (now ~0.6% and falling). Next update at :45.

Dev Patel  10:27
Perfect. I’ll tell Support team to watch the incident channel and keep customer threads aligned.

Sean Gallagher  10:29
Thanks all. After this stabilizes, let’s add a short snippet to the escalation playbook: threshold guidance for “declare incident” (multi-org + sustained >1% 5xx, etc.) so Support doesn’t have to debate this in real time.

Priya Shah  10:30
+1. This thread is a good example; we’ll link it in the playbook training materials (internally).
